content:
sophie: Hi team — incoming escalation from @luis (ACME). Reports sudden p95/p99 latency regression after yesterday's model performance rollout. Customer says API responses are timing out for some requests (~3x p99 increase). They’re on Dedicated.

luis: Confirming — we started seeing timeouts around 09:30 UTC yesterday. p95 went from ~120ms to ~290ms, p99 spiked to ~1.2s. Nothing in app changed on our side. This is blocking a live feature.

sophie: I pulled their request IDs and initial traces. Support note: requests are hitting model route model-xlarge-v1@v2026-03-14-quant. They were migrated to a new quantization profile (int8 + fp8 auto) in the rollout. Attaching trimmed logs below.

sophie: ```
[2026-03-14T09:31:12Z] req=abcd1234 route=model-xlarge-v1@v2026-03-14-quant kernel_select=auto quant_profile=int8_fp8 status=OK latency=315ms
[2026-03-14T09:31:12Z] req=abcd1234 kvcache_miss=true calib_status=failed quant_calib_fail=true fallback=fp16 kernel=matmul_fp16 latency=980ms
[2026-03-14T09:31:12Z] req=abcd1235 route=model-xlarge-v1@v2026-03-14-quant quant_profile=int8_fp8 status=OK latency=280ms
[2026-03-14T09:31:12Z] req=abcd135 kernel_switch=fp16 reason=calib_fail
```

sophie: Noting messages indicate calibration failures and kernel fallbacks to fp16 for some code paths, which would explain the large latency delta for a subset of requests.

@david: can you confirm whether the quantization profile rollout included an aggressive fp8/int8 kernel that has a slow fallback path ramping up?

david: Looking. Early hypothesis: the new profile enabled fp8 in 'auto' mode. For some sequence lengths or token shapes the runtime attempts an fp8 kernel then falls back to fp16 when calibration mismatches are detected. The fallback path currently does extra dequant/quant checks which are expensive and not amortized by batching. That explains p99 tail but not overall p95 jump unless the fallback rate is reasonably high (~10-20%).

mina: We calibrated offline against our eval set but saw a small bias on very long context (>2048) sequences — we added a conservative fallback threshold, but it appears the runtime’s auto-switch is triggering more often on real traffic distribution (prefix-heavy for this customer).

amaia: Ops note — the SLO alert triggered for p99 at 09:35 and auto-escalated. I’ve pinned the customer to the older variant temporarily using routing override while we investigate. Customer confirmed routing change reduces p99 back to ~160ms.

ops-bot: Route override applied: customer ACME routed to model-xlarge-v1@v2026-03-01-fp16 (manual override by amaia).

david: Repro steps for staging — use the following curl to reproduce high tail: ```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"model-xlarge-v1","version":"v2026-03-14-quant","input":"<prefix-heavy>...long prompt...", "max_tokens":256, "stream":false}'
```
Use request concurrency 8 and sequence length ~2200-3000. Watch backend logs for `quant_calib_fail` lines.

mina: I ran the above locally on a dedicated test pool and reproduced a ~2.6x p99 increase with the new profile, consistent with customer. I captured timeline where ~17% of requests hit fallback path. The calibration code returns `calib_ok=false` for certain per-layer scale heuristics.

sophie: Customer is ok with a temporary rollback if we can guarantee no quality regression. They want timeline for mitigation and a permanent fix.

david: Immediate mitigations we can implement now: 1) pin the customer to the fp16 variant (already done). 2) Roll back the global rollout for model-xlarge-v1 to previous quant_profile. Command: 
```
redwoodctl rollout abort --model model-xlarge-v1 --version v2026-03-14-quant --reason "p99 regression: quant fallback"
```
3) Add a per-route automatic fallback mapping so that if p95/p99 delta > 1.5x for 10m, route to fp16 variant. (I'll open PR to runtime).

mina: For medium-term fix: tighten calibration logic, add additional per-layer clamp heuristics and simulate customer prefix-heavy traffic in calibration set. Also add a ‘fast-fallback’ kernel path that does minimal checks and avoids expensive dequant/quant loops: if fallback triggered, use simple fast fp16 path that is less correct but much faster — then link to quality-monitoring to detect regressions.

david: Also add telemetry counters: quant_profile_attempts, quant_profile_fallbacks, fallback_latency_overhead. Forward these to Console as per-model metrics so SRE can alert earlier.

amaia: I’ll schedule a canary rollback for 10% of traffic first and monitor p95/p99 delta. If stable, fully roll back.

sophie: Action items for support/customer comms: 1) Confirm rollback completed and timeline. 2) Share workaround (pinned route) and ETA for permanent fix. 3) Offer 1:1 with eng if they want deeper postmortem.

david: Quick note: quality concern — fp16 variant has slightly higher perplexity on some prompts. We should run the customer's internal eval set in the QA harness after rollback to quantify any customer-visible quality delta. Mina can run that.

mina: Will run evals now and post results in this thread. Early expectation: negligible quality delta for their prompt distribution.

sophie: Thanks everyone. I’ll keep the customer updated: pinned route is live, we’re aborting rollout, and we’ll follow up with postmortem + fix ETA.

ops-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-284 created, priority=P2, assignees=[david,mina].

sophie: FYI — suggested followups: add regression guardrails to the rollout pipeline that disallow quant_profile changes without a staged canary (1%) and automated p99 smoke tests.

david: Agreed. I’ll prototype an auto-canary check that measures tail latency and fallback rate before allowing 100% promotion.

sophie: Closing loop when postmortem is published. Thanks all.
